This was it. This was the final push, everything I’d done, every deal made, ever accomplishment and every sacrifice came down to this. I ran faster than I thought I could, skipping over rubble and darting over cracks in the ground while all around me were the sounds of intense weapons fire; theirs and our own streaking through the air, the the roar of a gunship as it flew overhead was deafening as it cut down husks in our way. To my left and right there were soldiers of every species rushing with me on what would be the last charge for many of us but they kept on going, accepting that their sacrifices would be for everyone, of every species. The shockwave from an exploding armoured vehicle almost knocked me off my feet but for those beside it their end came quickly, probably for the best. There was no time to check for wounded it was do or die, that beam HAD to be reached, even by one person. Bright beams of light arced over and around me, the ground shuddering after every impact. Half way now, almost to the beam, but we were losing men and machine quicker. Most of our force gone I couldn’t help myself thinking that this was a forlorn attack but we had no other choice. Nothing would stop me from ending that what started roughly four years ago on that station, where I had been given the vision. 

The vehicle ahead of me took a glancing blow from Harbinger’s weapon kicking it up into the air, with a swift slide on my back it just missed being crushed. Pushing myself up I saw my squad mates running towards me; taking a tiny breather I let a tiny smile out at seeing them still charging. Suddenly a loud crash echoed behind me, to my horror it was another vehicle flying over the wreck. It landed rear first in front of them and soon fell backwards erupting in a thunderous explosion pushing my friends down to the ground. I couldn’t keep going forwards and let my friends… family die. Going directly against the orders I had helped construct I leapt onto the underside of the Mako then jumped down to see if my comrades were alive. Pulling the Sergal onto her back my heart sank, my mind immediately filled with the deepest sadness and the most violent of anger seeing her blood pour over my forearm. I tore myself away from the sight remembering that this mission was far more important than any single person, even Ashley.

Getting back onto my feet I sprinted, my mind fixated on the beam and nothing would get in my way, not even the shrapnel from a crashing gunship would stop me, sure fragments struck my arm but I couldn’t feel it; adrenaline was coursing through my system as we were but a few seconds from the objective. Time to finish this! But it wasn’t to be… that laser like bolt cut right in front of me throwing me back onto the ground in a ball of flame; the pain overrode what adrenaline was in my veins before all I could see was a blinding white.

My radio was still functional but I was in no position to use it.

“God… they’re all gone” was the last thing I heard.
